newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares climb as optimism returns.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares climb as optimism returns.

text.p: Slovenian shares edged higher on Wednesday on growing belief foreign investors would return to the market with a vengeance after their trading activity was blocked by the central bank last month.
"As soon as foreign investors are back, prices of most important shares will jump significantly as they are cheap compared to similar companies in the rest of Europe," one trader said.

The central bank four weeks ago blocked the inflow of international capital by ordering foreign investors to open custodian accounts at Slovenian banks if they wanted to trade in the country's shares.
So far none of the fully licensed banks has managed to prepare a custodian account scheme but said they planned to open the first accounts at the end of March.
"However, if foreigners decide to stay away due to high costs of the accounts or unpredictability of the central bank decrees, prices will decline," an analyst said.
Banks said the cost of the new accounts would be about 12 percent of the amount handled.
The blue-chip SBI index rose 5.68 points to 1,392.9.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded, easing 0.98 percent to 55,700 tolars on volume of 289 shares.
Overall seven shares rose, six fell, five were unchanged and eight were untraded. Turnover firmed to 55.9 million tolars from 48.3 million.
Ordinary shares of trader Kovinotehna were the top gainers, up 9.96 percent to 530 tolars on volume of 200 shares.
Preferred shares of Kovinotehna were the leading decliners, down 4.85 percent to 490 on volume of 375 shares.
